brief: Electric-bill inflation has turned data centers into a 2026 election issue: pause or moratorium proposals now appear in 20 of 36 governor races. BofA sorts the 36 states into four buckets. Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Oregon matter most for utility stocks. Arizona, Florida, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan and Wisconsin carry election risk the market is probably overpricing. A third group led by Wyoming, Minnesota, Colorado and Idaho has low risk, and Alabama, Arkansas and Oklahoma would be a genuine surprise if they flipped. In Texas, Governor Abbott shifted from AI booster to auditor, freezing permits as the state's 474 GW interconnection queue, 90% data centers, faces a December 10 ERCOT verification audit. BofA argues the real decision comes in 1H27 through that audit and the next legislative session, not the election itself, and expects capital to sort toward lower-risk states rather than stop, with existing projects grandfathered outside the Texas permit freeze. In Georgia, two contested utility-commission seats could flip control and enable a data-center cost-shifting framework regardless of who wins governor, the key risk BofA flags for Southern Co. Federal restraint on AI looks limited either way, and a permitting bill carries 50/50 lame-duck odds per Piper Sandler.
